easy.question: How many times a day should we brush our teeth?
easy.explanation: We should brush our teeth twice a day -- once after waking up and once before going to sleep -- to prevent cavities and bad breath.

easy.question: The ancient Indian practice of cleaning teeth with neem or babool twigs is called ______.
easy.explanation: Datun is the thousands-of-years-old Indian practice of using twigs of neem, babool, or karanj trees to clean teeth and gums.

easy.question: When should we wash our hands with soap?
options: Before every meal, after using the toilet, and after playing outside
easy.answer: Before every meal, after using the toilet, and after playing outside
easy.explanation: We should wash hands with soap at many points during the day -- before eating, after the toilet, after playing, and after touching pets.

easy.question: How many hours of sleep does a child need every night?
easy.answer: A child needs at least 8 to 10 hours of sleep every night to help the body and brain recharge.
easy.explanation: Good sleep helps our body grow, repairs tired muscles, and lets our brain sort and store everything we learned during the day.

easy.question: Which natural ingredient was traditionally used to wash hair in India?
easy.explanation: Reetha makes foam like shampoo when rubbed in water. Along with shikakai and amla, it was used for centuries to wash and nourish hair.

medium.question: Name three natural cleaning methods used in India for different parts of the body.
medium.answer: Neem or babool twigs (datun) for cleaning teeth, reetha and shikakai for washing hair, and besan with haldi for cleaning skin.
medium.explanation: For thousands of years, Indians used natural ingredients from plants for personal hygiene. Many of these are still used in villages today.

medium.question: How do elephants clean themselves?
options: They suck up water in their trunk and spray it on their body
medium.answer: They suck up water in their trunk and spray it on their body
medium.explanation: Elephants use their trunk like a shower -- they suck up water and spray it all over themselves. It is their own personal bath!

medium.question: Cats spend a lot of time licking their paws and ______ to keep clean.
medium.explanation: Cats are very clean animals. They lick their paws and fur regularly as their way of grooming and staying clean.

hard.question: Describe a healthy daily routine for a Class 3 student. Include at least six important habits.
hard.answer: A healthy daily routine includes: 1) Brush teeth twice -- after waking up and before sleeping. 2) Take a bath every day with soap and water. 3) Wash hands with soap before meals, after using the toilet, and after playing outside. 4) Eat three nutritious meals and two healthy snacks, including fruits and vegetables. 5) Drink 6 to 8 glasses of water throughout the day. 6) Play outdoors for at least one hour. 7) Sleep 8 to 10 hours every night. 8) Rinse mouth after every meal. Following these habits every day makes our body like a strong fort that germs cannot easily attack.
hard.explanation: A consistent daily routine of cleanliness, good food, exercise, and sleep is the foundation of a healthy, happy life.

hard.question: How did people in India keep themselves clean before modern soaps and shampoos? Compare old and new methods.
hard.answer: Before modern products, Indians used natural ingredients for cleaning. For teeth, they used neem and babool twigs (datun), salt, and charcoal powder. Today we use toothbrushes and toothpaste. For hair, they used reetha (soapnut), shikakai, and amla powder. Today we use shampoo. For skin, they used besan (gram flour) with haldi and malai. Today we use soap. For clothes, they used reetha water. Today we use detergent. For floors, they used cow dung paste mixed with mud, which also kept insects away. Today we use floor cleaners. The traditional methods were all natural, eco-friendly, and worked very well.
hard.explanation: Ancient Indian cleaning methods used plants and natural ingredients. Many of these traditions continue in villages and are now being rediscovered for being chemical-free.

easy.question: What happens to our heart when we run fast?
options: It beats faster and pumps blood quickly
easy.answer: It beats faster and pumps blood quickly
easy.explanation: When we run, our heart beats faster to pump more blood to our muscles. This is exercise for the heart and makes it stronger over time.

easy.question: Exercise makes our heart strong, our lungs breathe deeper, and our ______ work harder.
easy.explanation: Exercise strengthens our heart, improves our lung capacity, and makes our muscles stronger and more flexible.

easy.question: Which of these is a traditional Indian outdoor game?
easy.explanation: Kho-Kho is a traditional Indian outdoor game where one team chases and the other dodges. It involves a lot of running and is very exciting.

easy.question: Name three fun ways to exercise every day.
easy.answer: Playing catch-catch or tag with friends, skipping with a rope, and cycling around the colony are fun ways to exercise.
easy.explanation: Exercise can be fun! Skipping, cycling, dancing, yoga, climbing monkey bars, and playing outdoor games all count as exercise.

medium.question: Why is exercise important for our body? What happens inside our body when we exercise?
medium.answer: Exercise makes our heart pump faster, our lungs breathe deeper, and our muscles work harder. Over time, this makes our heart stronger, lungs more powerful, and muscles more flexible. Exercise also makes us feel happy and full of energy.
medium.explanation: The fast heartbeat, heavy breathing, and sweating during exercise are all signs that our body is getting stronger.

medium.question: Which of these is a safe place to play?
medium.explanation: Parks, gardens, school playgrounds, and building compounds are safe places with open space and no moving vehicles.

medium.question: In Lagori (Pittu), players knock down a pile of ______ with a ball and then rebuild it.
medium.explanation: Lagori (also called Pittu) is a fun Indian game where one team throws a ball to knock down a pile of flat stones while the other team tries to rebuild it.

hard.question: Why should we always play in safe places? Give examples of safe and unsafe places with reasons.
hard.answer: We should play in safe places to protect ourselves from accidents. Safe places include parks and gardens (open area with no vehicles), school playgrounds (designed for children with teachers nearby), and building compounds (familiar area with neighbours around). Unsafe places include busy main roads (fast-moving cars and buses can hit us), open terraces without railings (risk of falling from height), construction sites (falling bricks, sharp objects, and heavy machines), and ponds or rivers without adults (risk of drowning). We should always check if a place is safe before starting to play.
hard.explanation: Choosing safe places to play prevents accidents and injuries. Open spaces away from traffic and heights are the best spots.

easy.question: What should you do if a stranger offers you a chocolate at the park?
options: Take it and say thank you
Say 'No, thank you' and walk away
easy.answer: Say 'No, thank you' and walk away
easy.explanation: We should never accept food, sweets, or gifts from strangers. Politely say no and move to a trusted adult.

easy.question: You should create a secret ______ with your parents so you know if someone is truly sent by them.
easy.explanation: A secret code word is a safety tool. Only go with someone who knows your family's code word -- if they do not know it, do not go with them.

easy.question: Name two important rules to stay safe from strangers.
easy.answer: Never accept food, sweets, or gifts from strangers. Never go anywhere with a stranger, even if they say your parents sent them.
easy.explanation: Safety rules protect us from harm. We should also never get into a stranger's vehicle and always stay near trusted adults in public.

easy.question: Too much of which activity can hurt our eyes and posture?
easy.explanation: Too much time watching TV or using phones and tablets can strain our eyes and cause bad posture from hunching over screens.

medium.question: What is a secret code word and how does it help keep children safe?
medium.answer: A secret code word is a special word that only the child and parents know. If someone comes to pick up the child, the child asks for the code word. If the person does not know it, the child does not go with them and finds a trusted adult instead.
medium.explanation: A code word works like a key -- only someone the family trusts will know it. This helps children tell safe people from unsafe ones.

medium.question: Why is eating breakfast every day important?
options: Because it is a school rule
It gives us energy to start the day
medium.answer: It gives us energy to start the day
medium.explanation: After sleeping all night, our body needs fuel. Breakfast gives us the energy to focus, learn, and play throughout the morning.

hard.question: Why do both our body and mind need to stay active? Give examples of activities for each.
hard.answer: Both body and mind need activity to stay healthy. For the body, we should play outdoor games like Kho-Kho, cricket, and kabaddi, skip rope, cycle, do yoga, and dance. These make our heart, lungs, and muscles strong. For the mind, we should play thinking games like chess, solve puzzles and sudoku, and read books. Even Neha's Nani, who cannot run due to knee pain, does gentle chair exercises for her body and plays carrom and sudoku for her mind. She says a lazy body and a lazy mind both get rusty. When we exercise both, we feel full of energy and happiness.
hard.explanation: True health means keeping both body and mind active. Physical games strengthen the body, while thinking games sharpen the mind.

hard.question: List five important safety rules for children. Why is each one important?
hard.answer: Five important safety rules: 1) Never accept food or gifts from strangers -- they might be trying to lure you away. 2) Never go with a stranger even if they say your parents sent them -- use your secret code word to check. 3) Never get into a stranger's car or auto -- always say no firmly. 4) Stay close to parents or trusted adults in crowded places like markets and fairs -- it is easy to get lost. 5) Play only in safe places like parks and playgrounds, not on busy roads or open terraces -- this prevents accidents. Following these rules protects us from danger and keeps us safe whether we are at home, school, or outside.
hard.explanation: Safety rules are like shields that protect children from harm. Every child should know and follow them.
